nodes.summary: For a finite partially ordered set $P$ and each natural number $k$, let $c_k(P)$ be the number of $k$-element chains of $P$, that is, of $k$-element subsets of $P$ any two of whose elements are comparable; in particular $c_0(P) = 1$, counting the empty chain. The chain polynomial of $P$ is the polynomial $C(P, t) = \sum_{k \ge 0} c_k(P)\, t^k$ with integer coefficients.
nodes.title: Chain polynomial

nodes.summary: It is not true that for every finite distributive lattice $L$ every complex root of the chain polynomial $C(L, t)$ is real, where $C(L, t) = \sum_{k \ge 0} c_k(L)\, t^k$ and $c_k(L)$ is the number of $k$-element chains of $L$.
nodes.title: Stanley's Problem 20' has a negative answer

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every finite distributive lattice $L$, every complex root of the chain polynomial $C(L, t)$ is real, where $C(L, t) = \sum_{k \ge 0} c_k(L)\, t^k$ and $c_k(L)$ is the number of $k$-element chains of $L$.
nodes.title: Stanley's Problem 20' on chain polynomials of distributive lattices
